current_episode.title: Episode 587: Kier Gaines: Self-Awareness, Distress Tolerance, and the Mental Skills That Build Resilience

guest.titre: Licensed Therapist, Keynote Speaker, Content Creator
guest.entreprise_secondaire: It All Starts When You Do (book)
guest.bio_context: Keir Gaines started his career in presidential property management, then worked in attitudinal training for individuals furthest from opportunity including those released from jail and in substance youth treatment programs. He later moved into education and special education, building economic self-sustainability programs for children with disabilities, before realizing his gift for connecting people to feelings led him to become a licensed therapist. His work has reached millions through social media content creation, and he recently paused his therapy practice to focus on speaking engagements across the country.

pending_qa.q: What are the key qualities to look for when finding an effective therapist?
pending_qa.r: They need to be skilled, personable in a way you find palatable and helpful, and someone you feel you can trust. Keir Gaines emphasizes that personality and fit matter enormously because you're baring your soul to them. A therapist must be able to feel their way around the person—knowing motivational interviewing, CBT, and CPT isn't enough if you can't build genuine human connection and therapeutic alliance.

pending_qa.q: How should a therapist handle situations where a client is withholding the truth during sessions?
pending_qa.r: Keir Gaines tells clients: at any point if the truth is too much to bear, you can come back and say 'that's not really what happened, let me explain it now.' He assures them he won't judge them or penalize them—it only allows him to better help them. This frees people to think about their lie and come back with truth so they can co-problem solve together.

pending_qa.q: What are the limitations of using AI like ChatGPT as a substitute for human therapy?
pending_qa.r: While ChatGPT can give good insight and is brilliant for journaling and bouncing ideas, it lacks the pausing, reflecting, and silence that are medicine in therapy. When you cry, a therapist pauses and allows that silence to be another person in the room—ChatGPT fills space with words instead. AI processes ideas intellectually but doesn't process feelings the way humans do; it lacks human-to-human connection and touch, which are essential to therapeutic alliance.

pending_qa.q: What structural barriers prevent people from accessing affordable mental health care?
pending_qa.r: Therapy has become extremely expensive, especially in major cities like Los Angeles where good therapists charge four hundred to five hundred dollars per session and aren't on insurance. Insurance is a nightmare for therapists to deal with. Additionally, therapists are licensed specifically to individual states, so even virtual sessions cannot cross state lines. This means many people who actually need therapy are not receiving it because they cannot afford it.

pending_qa.q: How did a career transition from personal training to therapy reveal Keir Gaines' core purpose?
pending_qa.r: While working as a personal trainer, Keir Gaines realized he was naturally good at connecting with people and helping them through conversations—similar to how a trainer becomes a therapist figure on the gym floor. He recognized this wasn't just a side quality but something he could lean into and expand. His mother passing away when he was eighteen made him realize life's finitude and the value of donating his talents to helping others achieve meaningful change.
